conviction_note: A low-information print for a fully chartered owner. The arithmetic of the unchanged FY26 guide (EBITDA USD 260-280m against H1's 163.5m and a ~USD 60m/quarter adjusted run-rate plus vessel-sale gains and the four 7,000 TEU ships) points to a possible small EBITDA guide raise, and MPCC's own segment charter index is firm while the stock fell with the liners. Against that, the feeder peer Euroseas was sold on its 2H27 caution, and the Q3 dividend at 50% of adjusted profit on 10% more shares may be trimmed. So p_up 54 on a 6% move gives +0.48; the findings sum (+0.9) is larger because the guidance finding carries its own size.

findings.finding: The unchanged FY26 EBITDA guide of USD 260-280m implies only USD 96.5-116.5m in H2 after H1's 163.5m, while Q1/Q2 adjusted EBITDA ran USD 67.1m/65.0m. Q3/Q4 also gain the AS Angelina (and possibly Selina) sale gains and the four 7,000 TEU ships (USD 140m EBITDA over 3 yrs), so the release can lift or firm the EBITDA guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print that raised EBITDA guidance from 240-260m to 260-280m moved +6.2% (2026-05-27); the Q2 print with the guide unchanged moved -1.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at investing.com sits at USD 103m revenue for Q3, below the company's own implied H2 run-rate of 107-112m, so the published bar has not been fitted to the guide. The stock fell 13% from Oct 30 to Nov 6 with the liners, which is not what a market pricing a guide raise looks like. Caveat: a raise driven by sale gains is a one-off and may be sold, and management said at Q2 that only further vessel sales could change EBITDA guidance.
findings.independence: Q2 report: Angelina delivered Aug and Selina around Nov with no gain recognised in Q2; 7,000 TEU deal economics USD 180m revenue / 140m EBITDA (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=681739)

findings.finding: MPCC's own segment charter index, New ConTex, rose to 1,691-1,692 in weeks 46-47 (+1.8% MoM, +12.9% YoY), with 2,500-3,500 TEU momentum strongest. Meanwhile MPCC fell 13.1% from Oct 30 to Nov 6 alongside a Maersk sell-off (-12%), so the drawdown is liner-driven while MPCC's 2027-28 roll-over rates are firming.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog and coverage headlines: Q4 2025 (coverage 97%/58%) +8.05%; Q1 2026 (99%/69%) +6.2%; Q2 2026 (backlog 2.2bn, 85% 2027) -1.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: MPCC has traded with the liners: -13.1% from Oct 30 to Nov 6 against Maersk -12.0% and Hapag -4.5%, although its contracted tonnage-provider model does not share their freight-rate exposure. Had the market priced the firm charter market, MPCC would have held up like ZIM (+7.4%) rather than sitting near the NOK 24 placement price. Caveat: this is macro-to-company transmission until the release shows backlog and coverage up.
findings.independence: Contex week 47 (2026-11-19): 2,500/2,700 TEU 12-month assessments +3.0%/+1.7% over the month (https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/New-Contex-Commentary-2026-week-47.pdf); Euroseas said feeder rates rose 5-10% from the start of Q3 to mid-November (https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/boxships/euroseas-raises-dividend-profit-falls)

findings.finding: Euroseas, the closest listed feeder peer, reported Q3 on Nov 17 with a higher TCE and 90.6% 2027 coverage but said it expects 'supply-demand fundamentals to weaken from the second half of 2027'. ESEA fell 4.7% that day and about 13% to Nov 19, a read that the market sells forward caution in this segment on results day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MPCC fell 14.2% on its Q2 2024 print and 12.2% on Q1 2025 (capital allocation update); forward-looking caution has been sold hard here before.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: MPCC has drifted -1% since Nov 16. But the question will be put to MPCC's management on the call, and 40% of its 2028 days are still open (Aug), so a cautious 2028 comment would land as new. Caveat: MPCC's coverage is lower than ESEA's in 2027 (85% vs 90.6%), but its 2028 exposure is similar.

findings.finding: The dividend is under local scrutiny: E24 (24 Nov) reports a shipping shareholder saying MPCC needs more 'meat on the bone' on its plans after the dividend cut. At the policy's 50% of adjusted profit, a Q3 dividend on about 488m shares (after the placement) works out to roughly USD 0.035-0.04 against 0.04 for Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend cut from 0.05 to 0.04 at Q1 2026 coincided with +6.2% (the guide raise dominated); the payout-policy cut at Q1 2025 coincided with -12.2%.
findings.original_quote: Vil ha utbyttesvar: – Blir garantert spurt om. Shippingaksjonær mener det trengs mer «kjøtt på beinet» om MPC Container Ships' planer videre etter utbyttekutt. (Wants an answer on dividends: 'It will certainly be asked about'. A shipping shareholder thinks MPC Container Ships needs more substance on its plans after the dividend cut.)
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic of 50% of adjusted profit on the enlarged share count (Q2 paid USD 19.5m = 50% of 39.0m adjusted profit) has not been published as an expectation. The E24 piece is behind a paywall and Norwegian-only. Caveat: the article body could not be read, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Q2 report: dividend of USD 0.04 = about USD 19.5m total against adjusted profit of USD 39.0m; 44.37m new shares in July (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=681739)

findings.finding: Consensus for Q3 is USD 103.15m revenue / EPS 0.073 (investing.com), and MPCC has beaten that aggregator's revenue line on all ten prior prints (Q2 2026: 108.0 vs 101.7; Q1: 118.9 vs 104.6), so a headline beat is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ten straight revenue beats have produced reactions from -14.2% to +8.1%, so the beat does not decide the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a beat against a stale aggregator bar is the base case on every print. The bar is single-source, so this finding is capped small.

findings.finding: The EGM of 29 Oct renewed a 10% share-issue authority and added authority to take up convertible loans for 'potential strategic opportunities', so the release or call may carry a financing or acquisition step.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Jun 25 acquisition plus USD 375m loan and the Jun 30 placement at NOK 24 were followed by the stock trading up to NOK 28-29 by September.
findings.why_not_priced: The authority is public, but its use is not. Asking what the money buys: fleet renewal with chartered tonnage has been accretive here, which is why this is sized near zero with a wide range rather than as dilution.
